historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission accepted the Italian Consul General's offer of a monument to Christopher Columbus in the panoramic circle on Telegraph Hill, leaving the choice of sculpture to the Art Commission.

The Recreation and Park Commission agreed that the road up Telegraph Hill to Coit Tower be dedicated as an open public street, and asked the Director of Public Works to start the proceedings before the Board of Supervisors.

After the 1989 earthquake opened a major crack in the northern part of Telegraph Hill, threatening rock falls onto a development below, the Recreation and Park Commission declared an emergency to fund the rock's removal, estimated at $250,000.

The Board of Park Commissioners authorized Superintendent John McLaren to confer with the architect G. Albert Lansburgh on plans for spending the $10,000 the 1924-25 city budget allotted to beautify Pioneer Park on Telegraph Hill.

The Board of Park Commissioners made the final payments for the balustrade at Pioneer Park on Telegraph Hill: to P. E. Denivelle, its builder, and to the architect G. Albert Lansburgh, whose fee was 6 percent.

The Board of Park Commissioners approved, subject to its advisory committee of artists and architects, the Daughters of the American Revolution's request to set a tablet about 24 by 16 inches on the lower coping of the steps leading to Telegraph Hill, commemorating the first signal station there.

Pressed by the Marina, Excelsior, Nob Hill and North Beach associations to prepare plans for beautifying Telegraph Hill, including a suitable structure on top, the Board of Park Commissioners held the requests until its architects finished their preliminary studies.
